mi_corridor_the.blurb: The Corridor is a compact boulder cluster among the bluffs near Iron Mountain in Michigan's Upper Peninsula. It holds eleven problems, all on the friendly end: three at the easiest level, a handful around V1 to V2, and a couple of V3s at the top. Heights are modest, about ten feet on the problems described, so one or two pads is plenty. Because the grades are low and the blocks sit close together, it suits a relaxed session, a warm-up round, or newer boulderers. Expect a hike of roughly a quarter hour from the road, passing a cell tower and following a bluff face west.

mi_suicide.blurb: Suicide is a small bolted wall between Negaunee and Ishpeming, about twenty minutes from Marquette in the Upper Peninsula. Ten routes run from easy 5.7 to a single 5.12 test piece, with nine sport lines and one trad crack; most land in the 5.10 range, so it favors climbers comfortable on steady, thin face moves. Routes are short, around forty feet, with anchors at the top. The wall faces south and stays noticeably warmer than town, making it a handy spot for a quick session or training outing. It reads like an outdoor gym, a good bridge for those moving from plastic to rock.

mi_dream_the.blurb: The Dream is a boulder sector in the Lily Pond zone near Wetmore Pond, outside Marquette in the Upper Peninsula. A big blocky formation pushes out of a hillside toward a swamp, and it is the first group of boulders you meet after crossing the wet ground. Ten problems range from easy V0 lines to a few hard overhanging testpieces, with the prow on the swamp side being the standout. Landings can be soggy in places and some need tidying. The swamp is buggy in warm months, so fall, winter and spring are the better seasons to visit.

mi_man_in_the_chair.blurb: Man in the Chair sits along a ridge above Wetmore Pond, north of Marquette in Michigan's Upper Peninsula. Two south-facing walls, each over fifteen feet tall, hold ten problems that spread from very easy to the V5 range, with a few V2 to V4 lines carrying the best reputations. The stone forms shallow dishes and pockets, giving unusual movement. Getting here takes more effort than the nearby pond boulders: either follow the old railroad grade, which is flat but long, or push through the brush past smaller zones. Unclimbed faces continue along the east end of the ridge.

mi_swamp_thing_roof.blurb: Swamp Thing Roof is a large tablet jutting from a hillside near Lily Pond outside Marquette, forming a striking roof around eighteen feet wide. It holds many of the Upper Peninsula's hardest boulder lines. Of ten problems, a few are easy warm-ups from V0 to V3, but most are steep and powerful, from V5 and V6 up through several V7s, a V8 and a V10. A walk through the swamp is needed, and the roof lies a few hundred feet beyond The Dream. Bugs are bad in summer, so cooler months are better. Link-ups and traverses remain possible.

mi_rockport.blurb: Rockport is an old limestone quarry on the Lake Huron shore north of Alpena, in the Lower Peninsula. The east-facing walls run roughly 15 to 35 feet, mostly under 30, and the rock is loose and fossil-rich. Ten routes are listed, mostly trad with one top-rope and two short mixed lines; the rock climbs sit around 5.6 to 5.7 and the mixed ones around M4. Large loose blocks make rockfall a real concern, so cleaning by rappel before leading is advisable. The quarry sees few visitors and offers undeveloped potential more than classic climbing. Expect about twenty minutes on foot to reach the face.
